text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigerian military ruler General Sani Abacha tells opening session of peace conference of wives of African leaders that the continent should take its destiny in its hands.
- Long queues are back at petrol stations following announcement by oil minister Dan Etete that Warri oil refinery in the midwest is closed.
- A total of 45 firms, mostly indigenous companies, have so far applied to exploit marginal oil wells held by major oil companies but considered by them as uneconomic to tap.
- Work on the realignment of rail tracks being carried out by Chinese experts will be completed next month, says Nigerian Railways spokesman David Ndakotsu.

- A 50-member Nigerian private sector team leaves for the United States later this week to promote trade between the two countries whose relations have been sour over Nigeria's slow process of democratisation and alleged human rights abuses.
- The fedral government has received bids by five companies for oil exploration licences for about 20 open acreages.
- Nigeria may soon resume crude oil export to Romania going by a pact initiated by the Nigeria-Romania chamber of commerce to increase the level of trade between the two countries.
- Nestle Foods Nigeria Plc full year profit for 1996 exceeds forecast.

- In a bid to end the perennial problem of government's inability to fund its share of its joint ventures with multinational oil firms, the companies may soon forward a proposal that will enable them to solely finance oil projects.
- Families of 80 people who died in a Nigeria Airways plane crash in 1995 are receiving 185 million naira as compensation from state-owned National Insurance Corporation of Nigeria.
